name: Prague
tagline: City of a hundred spires above the winding Vltava
bestMonths: Apr, May, Jun, Jul and Aug
whenBlurb: Late spring and early autumn are mild and golden; December glows with Christmas markets. Avoid the packed midsummer heat and grey deep winter.

ourTake.lede: Prague is a walking city that punishes you for sleeping in, cross the Charles Bridge at dawn and you get it almost to yourself, by ten it's shoulder to shoulder. Give the castle a full morning and go beyond the courtyards into the smaller palaces. Skip the Old Town Square restaurants and eat in Vinohrady or Karlín where locals actually go.
ourTake.comeIf: You want a walkable old city of spires, castles and easy charm.
ourTake.skipIf: You need a beach, big luxury names or warm weather.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Four Seasons Hotel Prague
items.area: Staré Město (Old Town), on the Vltava riverbank
items.description: Three linked historic houses, Baroque, Renaissance and neo-Classical, on the river, with the finest Castle-and-bridge view in the city.

items.name: Fairmont Golden Prague
items.area: Staré Město (Old Town), by the river near the Jewish Quarter
items.description: A landmark riverfront grande dame reborn under Fairmont, the only hotel in Prague to earn two MICHELIN Keys.

items.name: Mandarin Oriental, Prague
items.area: Malá Strana (Lesser Town), below the Castle
items.description: A former 14th-century monastery turned serene Mandarin Oriental house, quietly hidden in the cobbled lanes beneath the Castle.

items.name: Augustine, a Luxury Collection Hotel
items.area: Malá Strana (Lesser Town), by the Augustinian monastery
items.description: Woven around a still-working 13th-century Augustinian monastery, cloisters, a monk's brewery, and Cubist-inspired design.

items.name: Andaz Prague
items.description: Set in the restored 1916 Sugar Palace, a design-led Hyatt house threading 1920s retro-futurist Czech art through the historic centre.

items.name: Almanac X Alcron Prague
items.area: Nové Město (New Town), near Wenceslas Square
items.description: A restored 1932 Art Deco landmark, the storied Alcron reborn, with its glamorous heritage dining room, Brasserie 1932.

items.name: The Grand Mark Prague
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A former Baroque palace with one of the largest private hotel gardens in the Old Town, classical grandeur, quietly kept.

items.name: Aria Hotel Prague
items.area: Malá Strana (Lesser Town), by St Nicholas Church
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A music-themed boutique below the Castle, each floor devoted to a genre, with a rooftop terrace over the red rooftops of the Lesser Town.

items.name: Alchymist Grand Hotel & Spa
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A cluster of Renaissance and Baroque townhouses restored with gilded, theatrical opulence, an ornate, old-world hideaway.

items.name: The Emblem Prague Hotel
items.description: A discreet contemporary design hotel a few steps from the Old Town Square, a rooftop lounge, a library, and a quietly modern hand.

items.name: Prague Castle (Pražský hrad)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Centre of Prague
Guinness World Records, largest ancient castle complex in the world
items.description: The largest coherent castle complex in the world by Guinness reckoning, a thousand years of palaces, courtyards and cathedral spires crowning the skyline above the river. A private early-access tour before the gates open lets a multi-generational family have the courtyards almost to themselves.

items.name: St Vitus Cathedral (Katedrála sv. Víta)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Centre of Prague
items.description: Nearly six centuries in the building, this soaring Gothic cathedral inside the castle walls holds the Bohemian crown jewels, royal tombs and the shimmering Art Nouveau windows Alfons Mucha designed. The 287-step climb of the Great South Tower rewards with the finest close view over the whole city.

items.name: Charles Bridge (Karlův most)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Centre of Prague
items.description: The 14th-century stone bridge lined with thirty Baroque saints, linking the Old Town to the castle side across the Vltava. Cross at dawn, before the crowds and buskers arrive, for the postcard light on the water and the towers, an unhurried moment that suits early-rising elders and children alike.

items.name: Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Centre of Prague
items.description: The medieval heart of Prague, ringed by pastel Gothic and Baroque facades, the twin spires of Týn Church and pavement cafes. A grand, walkable stage for the whole family, with the Astronomical Clock chiming on the hour.

items.name: Prague Astronomical Clock & Old Town Hall (Orloj)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Centre of Prague
items.description: One of the oldest working astronomical clocks in the world, dating to 1410, with a procession of the Twelve Apostles that draws a crowd every hour. Climb the Old Town Hall tower for a bird's-eye sweep of the square and its rooftops, a lift makes it easy for less mobile travellers.

items.name: Josefov, the Jewish Quarter
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Centre of Prague
items.description: The most complete surviving complex of Jewish monuments in Europe, its historic synagogues and cemetery woven into the Old Town. A guided walk through seven centuries of Prague's Jewish story is one of the city's most moving and reflective experiences for a family.

items.name: Old-New Synagogue (Staronová synagoga)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Centre of Prague
items.description: The oldest active synagogue in Europe, in continuous use since around 1270, and the legendary home of the Golem myth. Its austere early-Gothic hall is unlike anything else in the city, small, atmospheric and still a living house of prayer.

items.name: Spanish Synagogue (Španělská synagoga)
items.description: A dazzling Moorish-Revival interior of gilded arabesques, stained glass and a starry domed ceiling, the most sumptuous of all Prague's synagogues, part of the Jewish Museum. Intimate evening chamber concerts here are a discreet, refined way to spend an hour.

items.name: Old Jewish Cemetery (Starý židovský hřbitov)
items.description: Twelve thousand weathered headstones tilting against each other in layered rows, one of the most evocative burial grounds in the world, used from the 15th to the 18th century. A quiet, thought-provoking stop within the Jewish Museum circuit.

items.name: Malá Strana (Lesser Town)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Centre of Prague
items.description: Prague's Baroque quarter beneath the castle, its noble palaces, hidden courtyards and cobbled lanes barely changed since the 18th century. The perfect district for an unhurried private walk, with quiet corner cafes and garden restaurants for a mid-stroll pause.

items.name: St Nicholas Church, Malá Strana (Kostel sv. Mikuláše)
items.description: The supreme masterpiece of Prague Baroque, a vast green dome and a ceiling fresco so grand it seems to open the roof to heaven. Time a visit to one of the frequent organ or chamber concerts held beneath the dome.

items.name: Church of Our Lady before Týn (Chrám Matky Boží před Týnem)
items.description: The twin black Gothic spires rising over Old Town Square are the defining silhouette of medieval Prague, each crowned with a crown of mini-spires. The astronomer Tycho Brahe lies buried inside this soaring, dimly lit interior.

items.name: Loreta (Loreta Praha)
items.description: A jewel-box Baroque pilgrimage shrine near the castle, built around a replica of the Holy House, with a famous treasury of monstrances glittering with thousands of diamonds. Its cloister and carillon of bells make it a peaceful counterpoint to the busier castle.

items.name: Strahov Monastery & Library (Strahovský klášter)
items.description: Two of the most beautiful Baroque library halls on earth, the Theological and Philosophical Halls, with painted ceilings, antique globes and a cabinet of curiosities. The hilltop terrace outside offers one of the best panoramas of the spired city below.

items.name: Klementinum, Baroque Library & Astronomical Tower
items.description: A jaw-dropping 1727 Jesuit library hall of frescoed ceilings and historic globes, reached only by guided tour, plus a climb up the Astronomical Tower for a wraparound view over the Old Town rooftops. The small-group entry keeps it calm and civilised.

items.name: Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Centre of Prague
items.description: A row of tiny brightly-painted 16th-century cottages tucked inside the castle walls, once home to castle marksmen and later, briefly, to Franz Kafka at No. 22. A charming, storybook lane that delights children and grandparents alike.

items.name: Municipal House (Obecní dům)
items.description: The finest Art Nouveau building in Prague, a 1912 confection of mosaics, stained glass and interiors decorated by Mucha and his peers, wrapped around the grand Smetana concert hall. A guided tour of the salons, then dinner in the opulent French restaurant, makes an elegant evening.

items.name: Mucha Museum
items.description: The world's first museum devoted to Alfons Mucha, the Czech master whose sinuous posters of flowing-haired Slavic women defined Art Nouveau. A compact, intimate collection a short walk from Wenceslas Square, an easy, rewarding hour for art lovers of any age.

items.name: The Slav Epic by Alfons Mucha (at the Municipal House)
items.description: Mucha's monumental twenty-canvas cycle telling the saga of the Slavic peoples, some panels the size of a cinema screen, now on show inside the Municipal House. A single, awe-inspiring encounter with a national masterpiece.

items.name: Petřín Hill & Lookout Tower (Petřínská rozhledna)
items.description: A wooded 327-metre hill of orchards and rose gardens crowned by a miniature Eiffel-style tower with a 360-degree view of Prague. A gentle, green escape from the streets below, with a mirror maze and observatory that keep younger travellers happy.

items.name: Letná Park & Metronome (Letenské sady)
items.description: A wooded plateau above the river where a giant metronome now stands on the old plinth that once held a Stalin statue, and where you can count seven of Prague's bridges in one sweep. The seasonal beer garden with its Old Town view is a beloved local sunset spot.

items.name: Vltava River Cruise
items.description: The classic way to see the castle, Charles Bridge and the National Theatre reflected in the water, from a leisurely daytime glide to a candlelit dinner cruise at night. A private charter with a chef briefed on vegetarian and Jain preferences is easily arranged.

items.name: Kampa Island & the Lennon Wall
items.description: Nicknamed 'Prague's Venice' for its little canal and waterwheel, this leafy island beneath Charles Bridge holds a riverside park and the ever-changing John Lennon Wall of painted messages. A relaxed, romantic wander with the Kampa modern-art museum alongside.

items.name: Kampa Museum (Museum Kampa)
items.description: A converted riverside mill housing a fine collection of Central European modern art, strong on František Kupka and the Cubist sculptor Otto Gutfreund. A calm, well-curated space with a terrace café looking straight across the Vltava.

items.name: Wallenstein Garden (Valdštejnská zahrada)
items.description: A grand early-Baroque garden of clipped hedges, a dramatic frescoed grotto and bronze statues, hidden behind the walls of a palace that is now the Czech Senate, and free to enter. Peacocks roam the lawns, delighting children, and it is blissfully quiet.

items.name: Vrtba Garden (Vrtbovská zahrada)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Centre of Prague
items.description: One of the most beautiful terraced Baroque gardens in Central Europe, climbing in ornamental tiers up the hillside with statues and a view over the red roofs of the Lesser Town. A serene, little-known hideaway ideal for a private moment.

items.name: Estates Theatre (Stavovské divadlo)
items.description: The exquisite 1783 Classical theatre where Mozart himself conducted the world premiere of Don Giovanni in 1787, still staging the opera today in near-original surroundings. To hear Mozart in the very room he wrote it for is one of Europe's great cultural experiences.

items.name: National Theatre (Národní divadlo)
items.description: The gilded neo-Renaissance temple of Czech culture on the riverbank, its golden roof a landmark, staging opera, ballet and drama beneath a ceiling of allegorical paintings. A box for an evening performance is a grand, memorable night out.

items.name: Rudolfinum & the Czech Philharmonic
items.description: One of the finest 19th-century concert halls on the continent, whose Dvořák Hall is home to the world-class Czech Philharmonic. A ticket here is the connoisseur's choice for classical music in Prague, in a riverside setting of real grandeur.

items.name: State Opera (Státní opera)
items.description: A sumptuously restored neo-Rococo opera house near the top of Wenceslas Square, staging grand opera and ballet under a lavishly painted auditorium. The recent renovation returned it to full jewel-box splendour.

items.name: Black-Light Theatre Ta Fantastika
items.description: Prague's distinctive black-light theatre, where UV-lit figures float and transform against a black stage in wordless, dreamlike shows. Because it needs no language, it is a genuinely fun, all-ages evening for multi-generational groups.

items.name: Vyšehrad Fortress
items.description: A cliff-top fortress above the Vltava, wrapped around the neo-Gothic Church of Sts Peter and Paul, ancient ramparts and the Slavín cemetery where Dvořák, Smetana and Mucha lie. Far quieter than the castle, with sweeping river views and space for children to run.

items.name: National Gallery, Trade Fair Palace (Veletržní palác)
items.description: Prague's great museum of modern and contemporary art, in a landmark 1928 Functionalist building, with works by Picasso, Klimt, Van Gogh and Mucha's Slav Epic hall. The single most important art collection in the country, and rarely crowded.

items.name: DOX Centre for Contemporary Art
items.description: A sharp, converted-factory space for cutting-edge contemporary art, architecture and design, crowned by the Gulliver airship, a huge wooden zeppelin on the roof. The most forward-looking cultural stop in the city, with a good design shop and café.

items.name: Wenceslas Square & the National Museum (Václavské náměstí)
items.description: The grand boulevard-square at the heart of modern Prague, scene of the 1989 Velvet Revolution, closed at its top by the newly restored, palatial National Museum. History, shopping and grand architecture in one broad sweep.

items.name: Vinohrady
items.description: A stately residential quarter of Art Nouveau apartment blocks, leafy squares and the city's best independent restaurants and wine bars, regularly named among the world's coolest neighbourhoods. The relaxed, refined district in which discerning travellers actually want to spend an evening.

items.name: Riegrovy sady (Rieger Gardens)
items.description: A rolling park in Vinohrady whose grassy slope offers a classic view of the castle and spires at sunset, home to one of Prague's largest and most beloved beer gardens. A local, easygoing way to end a warm day.

items.name: Žižkov TV Tower (Žižkovská televizní věž)
items.description: Prague's tallest structure and its most divisive landmark, a 216-metre space-age tower with crawling giant baby sculptures by David Černý and a 360-degree observation deck. There's a one-room luxury suite and a restaurant near the top for a memorable, offbeat treat.

items.name: Karlín
items.description: A once-industrial district reborn after the 2002 floods into one of Prague's leading quarters for design, cuisine and cafés, anchored by the grand neo-Romanesque Church of Sts Cyril and Methodius. The place to see contemporary, creative Prague away from the tourist core.

items.name: Náplavka Riverbank & Farmers' Market
items.description: The revived Vltava embankment of vaulted cellar bars and moored boats, with a lively Saturday farmers' market of Czech produce, cheeses and street food. A genuinely local scene with castle-and-bridge views, and plenty of vegetarian-friendly stalls.

items.name: Havelské tržiště (Havel's Market)
items.description: The last surviving open-air market in the historic core, trading since 1232, with stalls of fruit, flowers, wooden toys and Czech crafts. A quick, atmospheric stop between the Old Town Square and the river.

items.name: Powder Tower (Prašná brána)
items.description: A soaring blackened-Gothic gate tower marking the start of the medieval coronation route to the castle, standing beside the Art Nouveau Municipal House in a striking clash of eras. A short climb gives a fine view down the Royal Way.

items.name: Kutná Hora & the Sedlec Ossuary
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Centre of Kutná Hora with the Church of St Barbara and the Cathedral of Our Lady at Sedlec
items.description: A former silver-mining boomtown an hour east, home to the soaring Gothic St Barbara's Cathedral and the extraordinary Sedlec Ossuary, a chapel decorated with the bones of tens of thousands. An unforgettable, easily private half- or full-day excursion.

items.name: Karlštejn Castle (Hrad Karlštejn)
items.description: Charles IV's fairy-tale Gothic fortress crowning a wooded hill just west of the city, once the treasury for the imperial crown jewels and the jewel-encrusted Chapel of the Holy Cross. The closest and easiest of the great castle day trips, lovely for a multi-generational outing.

items.name: Český Krumlov
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Centre of Český Krumlov
items.description: A storybook medieval town cradled in a bend of the Vltava, all pastel houses, cobbled lanes and a vast hilltop castle with its own Baroque theatre. Worth an overnight rather than a rush; a private car and guide turn the long drive into an unhurried pleasure.

items.name: Karlovy Vary
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Great Spa Towns of Europe
items.description: The grand 19th-century spa town of colonnades, thermal springs and pastel promenades where emperors and composers once took the cure, and the home of Becherovka liqueur and Moser crystal. A refined day of mineral springs, café society and a spa treatment for the whole party.

items.name: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise
items.description: The first restaurant devoted to Czech cuisine to win a MICHELIN star, a long tasting menu reviving 19th-century Bohemian cookbooks.

items.name: Field
items.description: Radek Kašpárek's playful, farm-driven modern cooking, Prague's most consistently celebrated star, and a MICHELIN Service Award winner.

items.name: Casa de Carli
items.description: Chef Matteo de Carli cooking the food of his Italian homeland, handmade pasta at the counter, and Prague's newest MICHELIN star.

items.name: Levitate
items.description: Christian Chu's Nordic technique laced with Asian spice, an inventive, individual tasting menu that won a star in 2025.

items.name: Štangl
items.description: Martin Štangl's manifesto for modern Czech cooking, foraged herbs and forgotten ingredients, and both a MICHELIN Star and Green Star.

items.name: Leaf
items.description: Barbora Šimůnková's sustainability-led kitchen, a MICHELIN Green Star for produce-forward, low-waste cooking.

items.name: Terasa U Zlaté Studně
items.area: Malá Strana (Lesser Town), below the Castle
items.description: A rooftop dining terrace with one of the great Prague views, the Castle and the red rooftops laid out below.

items.name: Alma
items.area: Nové Město (New Town), V Jirchářích, near the National Theatre
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery (the bar)
items.description: A day-to-night gastronomic complex, café, restaurant and one of Europe's most acclaimed bars, with a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand kitchen.

items.name: The Eatery
items.description: Confident, generous modern Czech cooking that has held its Bib Gourmand, a favourite of the local dining crowd.

items.name: Dejvická 34
items.description: A polished neighbourhood restaurant with Italian leanings, reliably good, and a long-standing Bib Gourmand.

items.name: Na Kopci
items.description: Czech and French cooking on a quiet hill in Smíchov, a warm, well-priced Bib Gourmand off the tourist map.

items.name: Výčep
items.description: Modern Czech cooking with a serious approach to Czech beer, a fresh Bib Gourmand doing the classics properly.

items.name: U Kalendů
items.description: An assured, ingredient-led kitchen that earned a Bib Gourmand in the guide's first Czechia edition.

items.name: U Matěje
items.description: A refined take on Czech classics in a smart neighbourhood room, a new Bib Gourmand for 2025.

items.name: Eska
items.description: A bakery-and-restaurant landmark of the Karlín revival, modern Czech cooking, wood-fired bread, and a MICHELIN listing.

items.name: Black Angel's Bar
items.area: Staré Město (Old Town), beneath the U Prince Hotel on Old Town Square
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery
items.description: A Prohibition-era cocktail cellar in a Gothic vault right on the Old Town Square, barrel-aged classics served on hand-made Moser glass.

items.name: Hemingway Bar
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery
items.description: A dark, intimate cocktail den devoted to Hemingway, rare rums, an absinthe fountain, and some of the most inventive drinks in the city.

items.name: L'Fleur
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery
items.description: Cocktails and Champagne given equal billing, exposed brick, chandeliers, candlelight, and one of the largest Champagne lists in the world.

items.name: Alma
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery
items.description: Prague's most decorated bar, wild herbs, foraged ingredients and pickled pine cones in the glass, in a converted former cinema.

items.name: Cloud 9 Sky Bar & Lounge
items.area: Nové Město (New Town), atop the Hilton Prague
credentials: Atop the Hilton Prague, a landmark high-level bar
items.description: A glass-walled sky bar and terrace over the Vltava, one of the few genuine high-level views in a city of low rooftops.

items.name: Terasa U Zlaté Studně
items.area: Malá Strana (Lesser Town), below the Castle
credentials: Atop the U Zlaté Studně hotel, a MICHELIN Guide dining address
items.description: A rooftop terrace tucked beneath Prague Castle, the Baroque rooftops and spires of the Lesser Town laid out at your feet.

plan.heading: 3 days in Prague, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Prague Castle and St Vitus Cathedral at opening, then the Golden Lane before the day tours arrive.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Descend through the Lesser Town to the Wallenstein Garden, then coffee at the Augustine cloister.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise, the Michelin room reworking old Czech recipes on Haštalská.

days.label: Day 2
days.title: The old town and the river

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Cross the Charles Bridge at first light, then the Old Town Square and the Astronomical Clock before ten.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Jewish Quarter, the Old-New Synagogue and the Spanish Synagogue, at an unhurried pace.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Field, the Michelin-starred room near the river, then Hemingway Bar for a late drink.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Mucha Museum and the Municipal House, then a private viewing of the Slav Epic if it is on show.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch at the Café Savoy, then browse the Pařížská maison houses before packing up.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A farewell dinner at the Alcron, the restored Art Deco room off Wenceslas Square.

items.name: Malá Strana
items.description: Baroque lanes below the castle, the most atmospheric, romantic base.

items.name: Vinohrady
items.description: Leafy residential streets and the best restaurants, for a local stay.

items.name: Josefov / Old Town
items.description: Central and historic but busy, for those who want everything on foot.

events.name: Prague Spring International Music Festival
events.note: The country's premier classical festival, opening with Smetana's Má vlast.

events.name: Signal Festival
events.note: A festival of light installations that transforms the historic centre after dark.

events.name: Christmas markets
events.note: The Old Town and Wenceslas squares fill with wooden stalls and mulled wine.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay in Malá Strana or on the quieter side of the Old Town away from the tourist crush; taxis are best pre-booked through your hotel to avoid overcharging, and the city rewards early mornings before the crowds reach the Charles Bridge.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: You arrive at Václav Havel Airport (PRG), about 30 minutes by private car into the centre, with a chauffeur handling the approach through the cobbled quarters.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: The historic core is compact and walkable but the cobblestones are unforgiving, so keep a private driver for evenings and anything beyond the old town.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Connectivity is strong; an eSIM works instantly and wifi is dependable, though the EU roaming zone covers Czechia as well.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: The Czech koruna, not the euro; cards are widely taken but keep some koruna for taxis and cafés, and a 10 percent tip is customary at restaurants.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: May, June and September give warm days and long light over the Old Town without August's heat; December has atmospheric markets but short, cold days. Avoid January-February for grey cold and July-August for peak crowds.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No non-stop from India; cleanest routing is via Munich or Frankfurt on Lufthansa (about 10h40m total), or via Zurich on SWISS, all with fine business cabins. A single European hub connection keeps it simple; the Baku routing on Azerbaijan Airlines is marginally faster but weaker in premium.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations needed; tap water is safe to drink. Prague is safe; the main nuisances are pickpockets and overcharging taxis around tourist squares, so use booked cars.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian food is straightforward and Indian options are good. Govinda and Dhaba Beas are dependable pure-veg spots; Jain requests are best pre-arranged as local menus lean onion-garlic.
